interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
Hello, I am EXPERT-EAU. I will now search the guidelines for management after a prostate cancer biopsy.

**GUIDELINE**
"e patients with suspected organ-confined disease. Strong Perform limited biopsy only, without MRI, in males with clear evidence of locally advanced disease on digital rectal examination or those not for curative treatment. Weak Combine targeted biopsy with perilesional sampling when MRI is positive (i.e. PI-RADS ≥ 4)."

**WHAT THE EXPERTS DO NOT SETTLE**
The experts have not settled on the definitive management strategy following the biopsy. The uncertainty lies in whether to proceed with active treatment given the ISUP grade 2 finding, and how to integrate the clinical findings (DRE suspicious nodule, PI-RADS 4) with the pathology result.

**WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE**
The documents must settle on the recommended next step for this patient, specifically regarding the initiation of active treatment following the ISUP grade 2 biopsy result, considering the clinical context (PSA, PI-RADS 4, DRE).

7.3.3.a
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.
7.3.3.a.1
Prostate-specific antigen monitoring after radical prostatectomy
Following RP, the PSA level is expected to be undetectable.

WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**
Findings: Focal, ill-defined hypointense lesion in the peripheral zone of the mid left prostate, measuring approximately 12 mm. Shows restricted diffusion on DWI and hyperintensity on ADC map. DCE shows early, focal enhancement. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Impression: PI-RADS 4 lesion in the peripheral zone, mid left. Clinical T stage: cT1c.

**pathology_report**
Findings: Histological examination reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, mid left. Summary: Histological progression from a negative biopsy to ISUP grade group 2 disease.
